rule: Synapse tools key, read through the frontmatter reader CHECK 16 uses, is exactly Bash and Write, and its frontmatter contains no Skill or Edit
description: plugin/agents/synapse.md is the runner agent that workflow scripts start to run one committed runner script. Its frontmatter tools: list is what grants it tools, so this fixture pins that list. The set_check reads the top-level tools key with extract_frontmatter_key, which runs check16_collect_entries, the frontmatter reader CHECK 16 uses in tools/policy_check.sh, and requires, in equal mode with expected_counts, exactly Bash and Write, each once. A tool added in any form the reader reads fails as an extra: a block list at any indent, a compact list, an inline flow list, a comma-separated string, or a second tools key. Each entry is compared whole; a duplicated tool fails its count, and a deleted tool fails as missing. A tools value in a form the reader cannot read fails the check and names the file, line and text: a quoted or indented key, a block scalar, an unclosed flow sequence, the key's text on any other frontmatter line, or an entry outside the tool-entry grammar. set_check is used because an added grant is the threat, and a presence pin can only notice deletion. The two frontmatter-absent consumers require that the substrings Skill and Edit appear nowhere in the frontmatter. The source pin sits on the body sentence that limits synapse to its input-file Writes and the one Bash call; deleting it is loud. What this fixture does not check: (a) what Bash and Write can do; the synapse runner gate hook bounds them, pinned by safety-synapse-gate.json, and the pin claims names, never capability or meaning; (b) grants from any other file, such as settings files or the workflow scripts that start synapse; (c) any other agent file; files is a literal list that names only synapse.md and is blind to newly added files.

source.pattern: Call no tool besides those Writes and that Bash.
